fact: App is Next.js 15.1.6 App Router (src/app/) with React 19, package name velocity-esim-frontend, using pnpm workspace and Turbopack for dev.
Scripts: dev='next dev --turbopack', build='next build', start='next start', test='vitest run'; no lint script defined.

All backend calls go through a BFF layer at src/app/bff/** (moved from src/app/api/** on 2026-08-13) because nginx in production proxies the entire /api/* prefix straight to the Express backend, so Next route handlers under /api were unreachable in prod.

getBackendApiUrl() in src/lib/backend.ts defaults to https://esim.uplisoft.com/api in every environment including next dev; set BACKEND_API_URL to point at a local backend (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4000/api).

backendFetch() in src/lib/backend.ts wraps fetch with cache:'no-store', unwraps the {status,data,error,message} envelope, and returns a discriminated BackendResult<T>; network/JSON failures collapse to a fixed message 'We could not reach the eSIM service. Please try again.' with status 502.
Session tokens (esim_at access, esim_rt refresh) are httpOnly cookies set in src/lib/session.ts; cookies use secure:true only when NODE_ENV==='production' so LAN/http dev testing still works.

callWithSession() in src/lib/with-session.ts runs a backend call with the access token, and on a 401 transparently refreshes once via POST /auth/refresh and retries; a second 401 clears all session cookies and returns 'Your session has expired. Please sign in again.'

There is no /user/me endpoint; the signed-in email is read client-unverified from the access token payload via readEmailFromAccessToken() in src/lib/session-identity.ts, which decodes base64url JWT-like segments (dev-auth.<payload>.<sig>) for DISPLAY ONLY and never as an authorization decision.

Middleware previously built redirect URLs from url.origin (resolved from the internal bind address 127.0.0.1:3020 behind nginx), sending production visitors to https://localhost:3020/signin?next=...; fixed by deriving all redirect URLs from getPublicOrigin(request) in src/lib/public-origin.ts, which reads x-forwarded-host/x-forwarded-proto.

src/lib/route-guard.ts guards prefixes /account, /checkout, /profile (redirects to /signin?next=<path>) unless the path is in UNGUARDED_PATHS: /checkout/return, /account/topup/return, /profile/deleted — these must stay reachable with an already-cleared or short-lived session cookie.

src/middleware.ts matcher excludes _next/static, _next/image, favicon.ico, og/; it also canonicalizes www.esim.uplisoft.com -> esim.uplisoft.com, forces https, and strips trailing slashes, redirect priority: canonicalize first (308), then auth guard.

Google sign-in requires NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID (must equal backend GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID) and the site origin must be an Authorized JavaScript origin in Google Cloud Console; Apple sign-in requires NEXT_PUBLIC_APPLE_SERVICES_ID which is a Services ID (NOT the app bundle id, NOT a Google client id) and must equal backend APPLE_SERVICES_ID.

A Google iOS OAuth client id (…apps.googleusercontent.com) was mistakenly pasted into NEXT_PUBLIC_APPLE_SERVICES_ID, which passed the SocialSignInButtons non-empty render guard and made the Apple button render then fail invalid_client; fixed by setting the real Apple Services ID com.uplisoft.velocityesim.web.

Google sign-in failed in production only with 'redirect_uri_mismatch' (shown to users as a generic OAuth policy error) because https://esim.uplisoft.com was missing from Authorized JavaScript origins on the Google OAuth web client; localhost worked because Google ignores the port for localhost origins. Fixed in Google Cloud Console, no code change.

src/app/bff/auth/social/apple/route.ts deliberately never sends authorizationCode to the backend, so a web-only Apple sign-in stores no refresh token and revoke-on-delete does not cover that identity; native/mobile sign-in is unaffected.

GET /orders/active returns a single order (backend allows only one live plan at a time) and expires a depleted plan as a SIDE EFFECT of being called; src/lib/order-groups.ts's resolveOrderSections treats /orders/active as authoritative over the /orders list for lifecycle status.

groupOrdersByLifecycle() in src/lib/order-groups.ts buckets orders into active/ready/history by lifecycle_status ('active'|'expired'|else=ready), sorts each newest-first by created_at, and demotes any surplus 'active' orders beyond the first into ready rather than dropping them.

PUT /user/card-details returns 410 Gone — saved cards are deliberately disabled; card entry only happens on Pokpay's hosted checkout, so /profile/billing only edits a billing address (GET/PUT /user/billing-address).

Top-up flow: TopUpPanel -> POST /bff/payments/topups/intent -> Pokpay hosted checkout -> /account/topup/return -> backend /payments/topups/provision -> redirect /account/:id?topup=1. The provisioning response cannot identify which eSIM was topped up (it returns the provider's top-up record and the payment reference only yields an ICCID), so orderId:paymentId is stashed in the esim_pending_topup cookie at intent time.
Only a 402 payment response is reported to the user as reason=unpaid; every other checkout/top-up failure reports reason=provisioning because a non-402 failure may have already taken the card.

PayButton (src/app/checkout/PayButton.tsx) navigates with window.location.assign to the Pokpay checkoutUrl (full-page nav, not a popup) because popups are unreliable in mobile and in-app browsers; a 401 from /bff/payments/intent redirects to /signin?next=/checkout?package=<id>.

The navbar profile icon is a static link (not session-aware) for both signed-in and signed-out visitors so public SEO pages can stay statically generated; the route guard in middleware handles bouncing anonymous visitors instead.

src/services/packages.ts and src/services/server-packages.ts share one mapPackagesPayload() so browser (via GET /bff/packages) and Server Components (via backendFetch('/packages') directly) render identical HeroPackageOption shapes; browser path never talks to the backend origin directly.

Tailwind theme defines a custom palette (ink #06262f, midnight #001f26, cyan #00d9f5, aqua #71efff, cloud #f4fbfd, mist #dff6fa, line #c7e9ef) and font families sans='Inter' via --font-inter, display='Plus Jakarta Sans' via --font-display; content glob is src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,mdx}.

Vitest is configured node-environment, include src/**/*.test.ts only (not .tsx), with @ alias resolved to src/; test files sit next to the code they cover (co-located *.test.ts), not in a separate __tests__ tree.

As of 2026-08-13 the suite was at 221 passing tests with 4 known-flaky pre-existing failures in landing.test.ts (x3) and hero-package-search.test.ts (x1), confirmed unrelated to changes by stashing and re-running on a clean tree.

Hidden, unlisted admin surfaces live at /xloginy (purchase/user/OTP dashboard) and /xerrors (sanitized backend error inbox with resolve/repair actions) — deliberately not linked from nav; both prefixes plus /bff, /api, /admin, /account, /auth, /billing, /checkout, /dashboard, /profile, /signin are in privateRoutePrefixes (src/lib/seo.ts) so they are Disallow'd in robots.txt and excluded from the sitemap.

velocity-eSim (mobile) has EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://esim.uplisoft.com/api compiled into shipped builds, and api.uplisoft.com does not resolve — so esim.uplisoft.com/api can never be repointed at Next; this is why the BFF had to move to /bff instead of nginx being reconfigured.

.env.production is committed to git on purpose (contains only NEXT_PUBLIC_* values, which are public by definition once bundled); update.sh deploys via git pull then builds on the server, so any env var not committed is simply absent in production — this is exactly how the Google button previously failed to render in prod.
Production runs Next on 127.0.0.1:3020 behind nginx (per update.sh / prod_redirect_localhost session); canonical host is esim.uplisoft.com, apex not www, enforced by src/middleware.ts.

Web Apple sign-in cannot currently support revoke-on-delete for web-only accounts (see f015); a real fix needs a per-client client-secret JWT, a client-id parameter on the Apple token exchange, and a record of which client minted each stored refresh token — noted as future work, not yet implemented.

PayButton, SignOutButton, Navbar CTA, and DeleteAccountCard buttons were all migrated onto it (commits 4ab945e..a3e70c2).

Phase 2 of the mobile-parity redesign (design tokens) added brandBlue #0B49B7, brandTeal #09C3BE, error #BA1A1A to tailwind.config.ts plus a mobile-matching type scale (display-lg, headline-md, title-sm, body-md, body-sm, label-caps, mono-data). The display font family changed from Plus Jakarta Sans to Hanken Grotesk; a mono family (Geist) was added. This supersedes f024's palette/font description.

Hanken Grotesk/Inter/Geist were declared as CSS variables in tailwind.config.ts and globals.css but never actually loaded — src/app/layout.tsx had no next/font import, so all three silently fell back to system fonts in every environment. Fixed by loading all three via next/font/google in layout.tsx and applying their .variable classNames to <body>. This corrects an implicit assumption in old fact f024 (the fonts were configured, not necessarily rendering).

Both admin pages (/xloginy, /xerrors) store their admin dashboard token in sessionStorage under the shared key 'velocity-admin-dashboard-token' — JS-readable, unlike the httpOnly esim_at/esim_rt user-session cookies (topics/auth.json). An XSS on either admin page could read the admin token directly; this is a materially weaker trust model than regular user auth.

xloginy/page.tsx and xerrors/page.tsx each independently reimplement their own login form, handleLogin() POST to /bff/admin/login, 401-triggered logout, and formatDate() helper — despite being identical logic, there is no shared admin-auth hook or component between them.

xerrors' buildSafeCurl() reconstructs a copy-pasteable curl command using a hardcoded base URL 'https://esim.uplisoft.com' regardless of which backend environment the error actually came from — the reconstructed curl always points at production.

src/app/checkout/page.tsx conditionally renders a 'Voice & SMS' summary row only when plan.voiceMinutes or plan.smsCount is set (matching HeroPackageOption's optional fields from ui-components-styling.json f035); data-only packages show Destination/Data/Validity rows only.

src/app/account/page.tsx deliberately awaits GET /orders/active alone and FIRST (its read has the side effect of expiring a depleted plan server-side), then fetches /orders (full list) and /orders/:id/usage together via Promise.all only if an active order exists — so the list request already reflects any expiry the active-order read just caused.

New hidden page /xpricing (src/app/xpricing/page.tsx) is a third admin surface: an editable data table over the backend's package pricing API (GET/PUT /admin/packages/pricing, POST /admin/packages/pricing/bulk-discount) showing originalPrice (read-only, Airalo cost), an editable retailPrice, an editable discount (percentage|flat + enable toggle), and a locally-previewed finalPrice per row. Bulk-discount panel applies a discount to selected rows or to every package ('packageIds: "all"') without touching retail prices, matching the backend contract exactly. New BFF proxies at src/app/bff/admin/packages/pricing/**, all using the backendFetch helper.

src/app/useAdminSession.ts extracts the token/login/logout/401-handling logic that f045 flagged as duplicated between xloginy and xerrors, and the new xpricing page uses it. xloginy and xerrors themselves were NOT retrofitted onto the hook in this session (still duplicated per f045) — only the new page avoids adding a third copy.

All three hidden admin pages (/xloginy, /xerrors, /xpricing) now share one visual system: AdminNav.tsx is a vertical icon rail (dark midnight/ink gradient, glowing active-state, usePathname()-based highlighting) instead of the old horizontal pill nav, and AdminLoginCard.tsx is a shared premium login form used by all three. ogImage.url (src/lib/seo.ts) has a manual cache-busting query param, ogImageVersion (currently '3') appended as ?v=. Bump this constant any time public/og/esim2you-og.png's contents change, or link-preview crawlers (iMessage/WhatsApp/Slack/Facebook/X) keep serving their cached copy of the old image indefinitely since the URL itself didn't change.

Destination pages (both the 18 static /destinations/[slug] SEO pages and the live client-rendered /destinations?country=XX view, f042/f043) now show a visible 'eSIM plans from EUR X.XX' price badge backed by matching Product/AggregateOffer JSON-LD (src/lib/seo.ts createOfferProductJsonLd, wired through createContentPageJsonLd's new optional `offer` param). New src/lib/destinationPricing.ts:getDestinationOffer(slug) fetches /api/packages server-side (Next fetch cache, next:{revalidate:3600}, so static pages get an hourly-refreshed price without a full rebuild) and computes the lowest priceNumeric for that slug's countryCode. Static pages with no matching packages simply render without the badge/schema (offer is optional) rather than showing a fabricated price.

/api/packages' `countryCode` field is NOT an ISO country code — it's a slugified country name (e.g. 'united-states', 'united-kingdom', 'united-arab-emirates', 'europe'). It matches destinationPages' slug (seo-pages.ts) directly for 15 of 18 entries; only usa/uk/uae differ from the backend's united-states/united-kingdom/united-arab-emirates (mapping lives in destinationPricing.ts's COUNTRY_CODE_BY_SLUG). There is no separate `region` field on packages — 'Europe' is just another countryCode value with its own real regional-plan packages, not an aggregate of individual country prices. All prices are quoted in EUR (`price: "€9.89"`), not USD.

Phase 1 of an Airalo/MobiMatter-inspired homepage redesign (page.tsx): deleted the abstract hero graphic (HeroVisual/DestinationBubble/FeatureCard) and the static non-live 'Plans' marketing section entirely, replacing them with a full-bleed photo hero (reuses /images/mountain.webp, already used elsewhere in Cta) + HeroPackageSearch over the photo + a new HeroDestinationChips.tsx (popular-destination chips from GET /api/packages/groups' popular array) + <DestinationBrowse urlFilters={{}} /> (the exact unmodified rails+grid+wizard component built for /destinations on feature/marketplace-rails, f071) embedded live. DestinationBrowse.tsx and HeroDestinationChips.tsx now distinguish a failed fetch from a genuinely-empty result: both track a loadError boolean (set in the catch of their fetchPackageGroups/fetchPackageOptions calls) and render a distinct retry affordance (DestinationBrowse: a WifiOff icon + 'Destinations couldn't be loaded' panel with a 'Try again' button; HeroDestinationChips: a small inline 'Popular destinations unavailable - try again' pill) instead of silently falling through to the same empty-state copy ('No destinations match these filters' / rendering nothing) a zero-result-but-successful fetch would show. Retry re-runs the effect via a retryCount state bump, not a full page reload. Also added DestinationBrowse's autoOpenWizard prop (default false, used only on the homepage via page.tsx) which opens the 'Help me choose' wizard immediately on mount instead of waiting for the button click; /destinations keeps the button-only default.

Fixed a real race condition in the homepage's auto-opened Help Me Choose wizard (f073): DestinationBrowse.tsx used to seed wizardOpen straight from the autoOpenWizard prop (useState(autoOpenWizard)), so on a slow connection the wizard could render before fetchPackageOptions() resolved, handing HelpMeChooseWizard an empty countries array -- any destination search then showed 'No destination found' purely from timing, independent of backend health. Fix: added WizardWelcomeIntro.tsx (branded splash shown via new showWelcome state) and two effects that gate the actual setWizardOpen(true) on BOTH a WELCOME_MIN_DELAY_MS (2000ms) timer AND the fetch having settled (!loading) -- a slow fetch extends the welcome screen instead of the wizard opening with no data; if the fetch ends in loadError the welcome intro dismisses without ever opening the wizard. The manual 'Help me choose' button also gained disabled={loading} for the same (narrower) race. New keyframe welcome-fade-scale in globals.css.

Redesigned the homepage's JourneyAndCoverage section (page.tsx): the 3 installationSteps now render as separate elevated border-outline/shadow-brandCard cards (stacked vertically) instead of one shared container with connector arrow-lines. The static usage-map.png coverage background image was replaced by new CoverageFlagMosaic.tsx (client component, fetches GET /api/packages/groups same as HeroDestinationChips/DestinationBrowse) showing up to 11 real destination flags + a +200 tile above the existing 200+/500+/99% stat bar. usage-map.png is now unreferenced anywhere in src/ but was left in public/images rather than deleted (no cleanup was requested). CoverageFlagMosaic is decorative-only: a fetch failure renders no tiles rather than an error UI, since the rest of the section works fine without it -- this is now the 3rd independent GET /api/packages/groups fetch on the homepage (alongside HeroDestinationChips and DestinationBrowse), compounding the known duplicate-fetch inefficiency from f073.

next.config.mjs's images.remotePatterns Wikimedia entry widened from a single literal hostname:'upload.wikimedia.org' to hostname:'*.wikimedia.org'. src/app/bff/country-image/route.ts's createImageResult() uses image?.thumburl ?? image?.url from Wikimedia's imageinfo API, which can resolve to either upload.wikimedia.org (originals) or thumb.wikimedia.org (thumbnails) depending on the specific image -- only the former was allowlisted, so next/image threw 'Invalid src prop ... hostname not configured' for any country whose capital-city image happened to come back as a thumb URL (first reproduced on /destinations?country=hungary). Any future Wikimedia subdomain this API might return is now covered by the wildcard instead of needing another allowlist entry.

Wired the backend's existing hasDiscount/retailPrice/discountType/discountValue fields (computed since 2026-08-23, /xpricing) through to the public web site for the first time -- previously only /xpricing itself consumed them; HeroPackageOption/ApiPackage in services/packages.ts never carried them, so nothing on the public site (Hero search, destination pages, checkout) could ever show a discount even when one was active. Added services/discountPricing.ts (hasActiveDiscount type guard, formatOriginalPrice -- reuses the current price string's currency prefix since the backend only sends price pre-formatted, discountPercentOff -- computed from actual before/after amounts not discountType/discountValue so it's correct for both percentage and flat discounts). Wired into checkout/page.tsx's total row and DestinationPlans.tsx's FeaturedPlan/CompactPlanCard: a -N% badge + strikethrough original price next to the current price when hasActiveDiscount(plan). NOT verified against real discount data -- the live catalog had zero discounted packages at implementation time, and setting one requires /xpricing admin login which the implementing session did not have credentials for.

Fixed a real bug in the web frontend's discount display (f077, same day): mapPackageToOption (services/packages.ts) only copied hasDiscount/retailPrice through when retailPrice > priceNumeric -- extra caution the mobile app's equivalent (formatRetailPriceLabel, velocity-eSim/src/currency/formatPrice.ts) does not have. An admin discount can mark a price UP (discountDirection:'increase', still hasDiscount:true per backend fact f107), and for that case (or any other where retailPrice ends up <= priceNumeric) the guard silently dropped the ENTIRE discount display instead of just hiding the percent badge. Removed the magnitude guard entirely -- web now trusts hasDiscount + retailPrice!=null exactly like mobile. discountPricing.ts's discountPercentOff now returns null (hiding only the badge) instead of the whole discount UI depending on percent being positive; hasActiveDiscount/formatOriginalPrice (the strikethrough) are unconditional on hasDiscount alone, matching mobile's formatRetailPriceLabel/formatDiscountBadge split exactly.

PackageGroupsRailId/PackageGroupOptions (services/packages.ts) and DestinationBrowse.tsx's RAILS/EMPTY_GROUPS gained a 5th rail, 'regional', mirroring a backend change to GET /api/packages/groups (E-SIM backend f114): regional/global bundles (Asia, Europe, Global, etc.) now come back in their own 'regional' array instead of being mixed into bestValue/unlimited/longStay alongside real countries. Rendered with the same generic rail card/Link pattern as the other 4 rails (label 'Regional & global bundles', appended last in RAILS) -- no special-cased tap behavior for regional entries.

HelpMeChooseWizard's step-progress header (days/data/destination) is now shown via BoardingPassStepperCard.tsx (exported component symbol still named BoardingPassStepper) -- a boarding-pass-styled card with two Lottie animations, plane-path.json and stamp.json, both statically imported from public/lottie/ -- replacing the old plain-text 'step X of 3' line, for visual continuity with WizardWelcomeIntro's Lottie loader. Mid-implementation the component's original filename, BoardingPassStepper.tsx, collided with the pure-helpers file boardingPassStepper.ts (differ only in leading-letter case) on macOS's case-insensitive filesystem, breaking both tsc and the real Next.js build; fixed by renaming the component file to BoardingPassStepperCard.tsx (component symbol unchanged) -- worth checking for on any future file added near an existing one whose name differs only by leading case. This repo has no component-rendering test infrastructure (no RTL/jsdom harness, only source-string/logic vitest assertions), so the new UI's logic was extracted into boardingPassStepper.ts and covered by boardingPassStepper.test.ts (8 tests) instead of a rendering test, leaving the component itself a thin wrapper. Visual render NOT confirmed in this environment -- next/font/google requires outbound network the sandbox lacks, so every route 500s in dev here (confirmed pre-existing on main, unrelated to this change); needs a human spot-check with normal network access.

BoardingPassStepperCard.tsx's step header is now circular nodes -- pending step number, a bouncing lucide-react Plane icon for the active step, or a stamped checkmark (CheckmarkStamp, still stamp.json) for a completed step -- connected by DashTrack components, each a row of 5 small dashes that light up together via a staggered CSS transition-delay when the preceding step completes, replacing the prior session's (f080) Lottie-scrubbed plane-path.json route strip, which read as static once actually seen running in a browser. frameForStep (the frame-scrubbing helper) no longer exists -- deleted from boardingPassStepper.ts along with its tests. Separately, picking a destination in HelpMeChooseWizard now waits 2000ms (showing search-package.json + "Finding your plans...") before calling onFinish -- a cosmetic pacing beat, not tied to a real async wait -- via a setTimeout read through an onFinishRef ref rather than a direct effect dependency, since the parent's onFinish prop isn't useCallback-wrapped and would otherwise restart the timer on unrelated parent re-renders; closing the wizard during the wait unmounts it and the effect's cleanup cancels the timer, so there's no orphaned navigation. Unlike the prior session (f080), this session's sandbox dev server could reach the network for next/font/google, so the full flow was manually verified live in a browser end to end.

HelpMeChooseWizard's trip-length/data-need answers were silently dropped whenever the user picked a specific country (the normal path) -- only the 'Skip - show all matching destinations' exit (WizardResult kind:'filters') ever reached wizardFiltersToQueryParams; DestinationBrowse.tsx's handleWizardFinish navigated a country pick with router.push(`/destinations?country=${code}`) alone, and DestinationPlans.tsx (the per-country page) had no mechanism to read filter query params at all -- it showed every plan for the country regardless of what the wizard asked. Fixed: WizardResult's 'country' variant now also carries days/data (HelpMeChooseWizard.tsx); wizardFiltersToQueryParams (destinationFilters.ts) takes a plain {days,data} instead of a WizardResult so both branches can call it; handleWizardFinish appends the filter params alongside ?country=; page.tsx forwards the same daysMin/daysMax/dataMin/dataMax/unlimited params it already parsed for DestinationBrowse to the new DestinationPlans searchFilters prop; DestinationPlans applies matchesDestinationFilters (already used by the all-destinations grid) on top of its country match, ahead of the page's own local unlimited/fixed/short/medium/long filter+sort UI. A direct /destinations?country=X link with no filter params is unaffected (parseDestinationFiltersFromParams defaults to no constraint).

Homepage JourneyAndCoverage (page.tsx) was replaced by HowItWorks, a full-width section: the "Where Will You Go Next?" coverage column (heading, CoverageFlagMosaic, 200+/500+/99% stat bar, "View All Destinations" button) was deleted entirely, not restyled -- CoverageFlagMosaic.tsx (f075) is now deleted as dead code, only ever used there. "3 Simple Steps" is now three fanned real-device phone mockups (PhoneFrame + ChoosePlanScreen/ScanInstallScreen/ConnectedScreen) instead of icon cards: ChoosePlanScreen recreates the real marketplace UI using an actual user-supplied screenshot (public/images/how-it-works-marketplace.jpg) as its hero-photo background plus real country rows with FROM €x.xx pricing; ScanInstallScreen shows a real, statically pre-generated QR code (public/images/qr-esim-uplisoft.svg, encodes https://esim.uplisoft.com, generated once via api.qrserver.com and committed as a static asset rather than hot-linked at runtime); ConnectedScreen mirrors the mobile app's MyEsimsScreen/dashboardData.ts copy conventions (active/expired pill, data-used/days-left, "eSim2you · Data plan"). All flags use real flagcdn.com/w80/<code>.png images (matching the site's existing flagUri convention), not emoji. Design was iterated via an HTML mockup file under .superpowers/brainstorm/ (not committed) instead of the browser visual companion. One real bug caught during live verification: the real screenshot already has "Stay Connected / Anywhere" baked into its pixels, and an early pass also drew that as an HTML text overlay on top of it, producing visibly doubled/ghosted text -- fixed by dropping the overlay and letting the photo's own headline show through the gradient. src/app/journey-and-coverage.test.ts renamed to how-it-works.test.ts and rewritten for the new structure.

DestinationBrowse.tsx's "All destinations" grid (215 countries) is now collapsible: collapsed by default to the first DESTINATIONS_COLLAPSED_COUNT=20 of filteredCountries, with a "Show all N destinations" / "Show less" toggle button (new showAllDestinations state) below the grid. The cap is skipped entirely while gridSearch has a non-empty query (isGridSearching) -- typing in "Search all destinations..." always shows every match, not just the first 20, so searching never hides a result the query matched. Popular/Best value/Unlimited/Long stay/Regional rails above this grid are unaffected -- only the flat all-countries grid was capped.

topics/troubleshooting.json exceeded its ~10KB budget (12.1KB, 13 entries). Split into troubleshooting.json (auth/routing/env/deploy incidents: redirect-localhost, BFF /api collision, Apple/Google sign-in, missing env, PH logo, 8 entries) and troubleshooting-destinations.json (/destinations page, Help Me Choose wizard, pricing/discount display bugs, 5 entries). brain.json's route table and index.json's keyword map updated to route to both; no facts were deleted, only the topic-file grouping changed.

Added feedAI/check-health.sh (run from repo root): flags topics/*.json over the ~10KB MAINTAIN.md budget and commits since brain.json's sync.date that never touched feedAI/ (drift proxy, threshold >5 flags STALE -- the 2026-08-19 incident was 20 such commits). Nonzero exit on either failure. Wired into README.md's load protocol as step 0. Same script also copied into E-SIM backend and velocity-eSim's feedAI/.

Fourth hidden admin page, /xnotificationy (admin-notifications.test.ts, layout.tsx, page.tsx), was built (commits a9e7bc5, 750a2f2) but never documented in feedAI. Standard AdminNav/AdminLoginCard/useAdminSession shell (same pattern as xloginy/xerrors/xpricing/xversion) around CRUD for the backend's NotificationMessage model plus a per-row Send button, proxied through src/app/bff/admin/notifications/route.ts, [id]/route.ts, and [id]/send/route.ts to the backend's E-SIM backend f117 endpoints (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/admin/notifications, POST /api/admin/notifications/:id/send). fact: /xloginy's main dashboard (page.tsx) picked up pagination controls (page/pageSize selectors + prev/next, one set each for purchases/users/OTP requests) matching the backend's new paginated GET /api/admin/dashboard (E-SIM backend f118) -- bff/admin/dashboard/route.ts forwards the pagination query params through unchanged. Two same-day 'dashboard UI polish' follow-up commits refined this further (visual/layout only, no new endpoints or params).

Extended feedAI/check-health.sh with a third check: files added since brain.json sync.date whose basename never appears anywhere in feedAI/ (facts.jsonl, brain.json, topics/*.json) -- a content-aware proxy for 'a feature shipped undocumented,' the exact class of gap that let E-SIM-frontend's /xnotificationy admin page go unmentioned for 2 commits until a manual cross-repo audit caught it. Heuristic, not proof: short/generic basenames (<4 chars) are skipped, and a hit means 'check this,' not 'this is definitely wrong.' Nonzero exit joins the existing budget/staleness checks.

Added feedAI/install-hooks.sh, wired into package.json's postinstall (runs on every `pnpm install`). It copies feedAI/git-hooks/pre-commit into .git/hooks/pre-commit if missing or stale, closing the gap where the pre-commit gate only protected commits made from a machine someone had installed it on by hand -- a fresh clone, a new contributor, or CI now gets the hook automatically on first `pnpm install`. Safe no-op if .git doesn't exist (e.g. a Docker build context).
